Keysight Technologies Inc reported third quarter 2026 revenue of $1.85 billion, representing a growth rate of 36.5% compared to the prior year period [D1]. The company delivered GAAP net income of $397 million, which translates to diluted earnings per share of $2.30, significantly exceeding analyst expectations of $2.16 per share [D1]. This strong performance was driven by record orders totaling $2.09 billion, a 56% increase year over year, with the Communications Solutions Group leading growth in commercial communications and aerospace markets [D1]. Management raised its full-year fiscal 2026 outlook, projecting fourth quarter revenue between $1.93 billion and $1.95 billion based on a weighted diluted share count of approximately 172 million shares [D1]. Operating margin expanded to 33.2%, surpassing the long-term target range of 31% to 32% due to disciplined cost management and revenue leverage [D3]. Free cash flow generation reached $403 million, providing financial flexibility while the company continued its share repurchase program with a recent purchase of approximately 640,000 shares for a total consideration of $210 million [D3].

The market is arguing about the sustainability of current growth rates given emerging supply chain constraints that management describes as a governor on near-term revenue conversion [D3]. While demand remains robust with a rolling 12-month funnel at an all-time high, executives caution that the supply environment is less flexible than a year ago and may limit the ability to convert backlog into revenue for the next several quarters [D4]. Analysts have noted that one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 artificially boosted profitability and will not repeat, creating a higher comparison bar for future periods [D3]. Additionally, there is scrutiny regarding whether the substantial gap between guidance and analyst forecasts can be maintained if supply constraints persist or if demand durability holds up against potential economic headwinds [D2]. The stock has gained 8.5% over the past four weeks to close at $321.87, with a mean price target of $418.42 indicating a potential upside of 30% according to Wall Street analysts [D5].

The plan therefore involves maintaining focus on deconstraining the supply chain through deeper engagement with suppliers and taking an 18-month-plus view on supply chain planning to accommodate high-demand new product introductions [D4]. Management intends to realize 80% to 90% of the $100 million in cost synergies from recent acquisitions on a run-rate basis by the end of the fiscal year, which will support margin expansion even as revenue conversion faces supply limitations [D3]. The company is also investing in strategic positioning with hyperscalers and advancing its portfolio for emerging markets such as 6G, where the total addressable market is projected to exceed that of the 5G cycle [D4]. Furthermore, Keysight is expanding its research collaborations, such as a partnership with the Centre for Assuring Autonomy at the University of York to advance AI safety assurance for software-defined vehicles, to support long-term innovation and customer trust in complex engineering challenges [D7].
